research_analysis.exact_observed_hook: "Did you know when Steve Jobs launched the iPad, he put a price on a giant screen behind him, and he left it there while he talked?"
research_analysis.visual_hook: Archival-style shot of a presenter on a keynote stage against a dark purple backdrop, hands clasped, smiling.
research_analysis.narrative_structure: Question hook about an odd choice, then 'it was the wrong price, on purpose' at 0:08, then the story in order, then the principle named in plain words in the last third, then a follow line.
research_analysis.viral_mechanism: A 'did you know X did a strange thing' question, followed inside ten seconds by 'on purpose'. The explanation is held back until the story is finished, so the viewer has to stay to learn why.
research_analysis.observed_evidence: 5.0M views on an 8K-follower account, 150.1x the creator's 33.2K median. 52.8s. Word-by-word subtitles. About 16 cuts of archival and stock footage. The principle is stated only from 0:36.
research_analysis.performance_hypothesis: Hypothesis: 'on purpose' turns a trivia fact into a puzzle, and viewers who finish feel they learned a trick they can spot elsewhere, so they send it to a friend the next time they see a price board. The small account size suggests the format carried it, not the creator.
research_analysis.why_this_format_fits_alex: It shows marketing knowledge through one concrete example instead of tips, which the audit says is missing from his feed (zero of nine recent Reels show his work). Filming a real board himself keeps it honest and cheap, and the voiceover over b-roll plays to his delivery.
research_analysis.originality_changes: Borrowed: question hook, 'on purpose' turn, principle named last. New: the subject is an ordinary coffee menu Alex films and does the arithmetic on, there is no archival footage, no founder story, and the script admits he cannot prove intent.

alex_adaptation.concept: Alex stands at a real coffee shop menu board, does the subtraction between small, medium and large on camera, and shows that the medium is priced to make the large feel like the smart choice. He names the decoy effect only at the end and admits he cannot prove the shop meant it.
alex_adaptation.target_audience: People 18-34 who like 'now I can't unsee it' explanations; small-business owners who set their own prices.
alex_adaptation.primary_emotion: Curiosity, then the small satisfaction of catching a trick
alex_adaptation.first_frame: Tight handheld shot of a three-size coffee menu board, Alex's finger already pointing at the middle price.
alex_adaptation.first_spoken_line: Did you know the medium at this coffee shop is on the menu so you won't buy it?

production.location: Any local coffee shop, smoothie bar or movie theater concession with three sizes on a visible price board. Ask the staff before filming the board.
props: One large drink he actually buys
shot_list: Close-up of the board with finger pointing at the medium
Finger slide across the three prices
Selfie in line with board over shoulder
b_roll: Extra 5 seconds of the board with no hand, for the bracket graphics
production.editor_instructions: Only shoot this if the medium-to-large gap is clearly smaller than the small-to-medium gap. If it is not, find another board. Replace both {{REAL}} tokens with the number read off the board. Record the voiceover in one pass in the car right after filming so the tone matches. Word-by-word captions in the lower third, graphics on the board in the upper half. Do not show staff faces.

variants_to_test: Alternate hook: 'Nobody at this coffee shop is supposed to order the medium.'
Alternate payoff: He ordered the medium out of spite
testing.promotion_decision: Brand fit 3: promote at 48h if views are at least 3x his trailing median and follows per 1,000 reached is in his top quartile; if follows are high under 6,000 views, re-film only the first 4 seconds with an alternate hook.
follow_up_variations_if_successful: Movie theater popcorn sizes, same arithmetic on camera
A gym's three membership tiers on its own website (screen recording)
A car wash menu with four packages: which one is the decoy

creative_confidence.rationale: The arithmetic is checkable by any viewer, the 'Large, please' beat gives it a joke in the middle, and it tells a new viewer what Alex does without a pitch. It is a voiceover explainer, a format he has not proven on Instagram.
uncertainties: Two {{REAL}} tokens: the price gap must come from the board he films
Needs a board where the gap pattern actually holds
He cannot prove the shop's intent and the script says so; do not edit that line out
Voiceover formats are untested for him
